part2.question: A time when you were stuck in a traffic jam for a very long time

segments.v: I want to talk about a big traffic jam last October. I was on the bus going home from my extra class. It was about 6 pm. Suddenly there was a big storm and many streets were flooded. The traffic stopped and my bus could not move. Usually it takes 25 minutes but that day it took three hours. I tried to do my homework but the bus was too crowded. So I talked with an old woman. She told me about floods in the past. I also looked at people pushing their motorbikes in the water. I felt angry and worried because my phone battery was low. But later I felt it was funny. When I got home, I was very wet and tired.

fluency.band6: Events in order; verb choice error.
fluency.band9: Time and cause (storm) → numbers (25 minutes → 3 hours) → what the speaker did (failed homework, conversation, observation) → a kind act → changing feelings → funny ending.

grammar.band6: “I looked at people pushing their motorbikes” (watched).
grammar.band9: Relative clause with “when” for background (right in the middle of rush hour, when a sudden storm hit…), “so… that”, participle phrases (some of them laughing, some clearly furious), and “ended up + V-ing”.

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 “I looked at people pushing…” should be “I watched people…” (watch for moving scenes). Band 9 sets the scene with numbers, describes vivid details and a kind act, and traces a change in feelings.
